17:45 Local Time, 12:15 GMT: The bowlers have endured a nightmare across both the ODI and T20I series, with little respite in either format. India chased down 405 and the West Indies overhauled 351 in the ODIs, before the Windies pulled off a 250-run chase in Ranchi, making it a relentlessly tough run for the bowlers across both formats. They have been reduced to mere bowling machines over the past three weeks. And on that note, hello and welcome to our coverage of the final game of the tour! It’s India taking on the West Indies at one of the country’s coolest cricketing venues - the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru..

Shai Hope has led the West Indies' charge with the bat, topping the charts in the T20I series with 261 runs. Sherfane Rutherford has been not far behind, piling up 221 runs to emerge as another key contributor. Hope has gone on to register two hundreds in the series, both of which have come in victories, a testament to the rich vein of form he has been in. For India, it has been more of a collective effort with the bat, though the returns have been mixed. The batters have blown hot and cold across the four matches, with consistency proving elusive.

Bengaluru has had its fair share of rain over the past few days, and there is a forecast for more showers tonight. That said, the Chinnaswamy Stadium boasts one of the best drainage systems around, which should help minimise delays and ensure that even if the rain does make an appearance, we could still have plenty of action on offer. Stay around for the toss and teams..

17:55 Local Time, 12:25 GMT: "Rain reduced to a steady drizzle. Covers still on. No work being done. No sight of the two teams either. Only about 20% of the seats are occupied with an hour to the scheduled start," pings Deepu Narayanan from the ground. He also throws in a stat - "The last international match at this venue began exactly two years to this day on a rainy morning and India were bowled out for 46."

Stat: West Indies featured in the inaugural Test at this venue in 1974/75 and played here again in 1978/79. But remarkably, since then they have only played just once here - against Sri Lanka in their victorious 2016 WT20 campaign. Only Daren Sammy from that playing XI ten years ago is with the current side in any capacity.

18:15 Local Time, 12:45 GMT: FYI, the two teams arrived a few minutes ago. But they have not started their warm-up drills because it's still raining and the covers are in place. The toss will surely be delayed given the current conditions. "Still only a drizzle, the kind where play would have continued had they been out in the middle," latest update from Deepu.
Bibek: At the stadium currently and there's a big patch of dark cloud right above the stadium. Fingers crossed.

18:30 Local Time, 13:00 GMT: The toss has been delayed. The drizzle has also picked up pace, it is a heavier now. "Stands about 50% filled," pings Deepu, and they are being entertained by the DJ. The two teams are in the dressing room looking quite relaxed and waiting for the rain to stop.
We will start losing overs after 30 minutes of lost time; latest start for a 5-over game is 9:41 PM - official scorer informs.

vinay : After such an entertaining series, a rain-affected decider would be a disappointing ending. Both teams have fought hard to reach 2-2, and fans deserve a complete contest at Chinnaswamy. Hopefully, the weather gives cricket a chance tonight.

Nelson Pynadathu Rumjit: The rain may have stopped the toss, but it can’t dampen the spirit of cricket fans! Every passing minute makes the wait more intense. Will the skies clear soon, or will rain steal the show? Let’s hope for a quick toss and a thrilling match ahead! Who else is eagerly waiting for the action to begin?
Pawan: A 2-2 series decider deserves a full game! Chinnaswamy has the best drainage in the world, so let’s hope the ground staff works their magic soon. We need a winner, not a washout!

Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, no run, a run-out chance, and Shreyas Iyer survives. He heaved across the line against this full length delivery, and gets an inside-edge onto the pad. Sets off for a single without knowing where the ball exactly is. Tilak too is hesitant - starts to run and then aborts. Shai Hope is quick to move across and gather the ball. Iyer was way outside the crease and given up, but Hope couldn't nail a direct-hit at his end. Would have been curtains for the Indian captain otherwise
Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, wide, fired down the leg-side and that's a wide ball

Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, FOUR, finally connects one. Gudakesh Motie goes full and Shreyas Iyer smashes it over the bowler's head as the ball almost goes the distance, just bounces in front of the rope
Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, FOUR, back-to-back boundaries. Drifting on the pads, Shreyas Iyer shuffles across and flicks it over backward square leg for four more. Much needed for him and India

Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, 3 runs, dropped near mid-off! Shreyas Iyer goes for the aerial route by swinging through the line, and miscues it completely. Rutherford charges in from the deep and tries to grab it, but the ball hits him on the chest. An overthrow allows them to come back for the third run. Rutherford overran that and got himself into a tangle, tried to adjust and take it close to the body but made a complete mess
Gudakesh Motie to Tilak Varma, 1 run, heaved towards deep mid-wicket by Tilak Varma for a single
It has started drizzling again
Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, wide, full and wide outside off, misses the tramline comfortably
Gudakesh Motie to Shreyas Iyer, 1 run, low full toss around middle and leg, Shreyas Iyer swings hard, only to get an inside edge towards short fine leg
The drizzle is getting heavier, but they continue playing
Keemo Paul [1.0-0-14-1] is back into the attack
Keemo Paul to Shreyas Iyer, THATS OUT!! Caught!!

Keemo Paul to Shreyas Iyer, out Caught by Shamar Joseph!! A rusty knock by Shreyas Iyer comes to an end. Wasn't quite in his elements tonight. This was banged in short by Keemo Paul and Shreyas Iyer went for a pull. Miscues it towards deep mid-wicket, and Shamar holds on to another safe catch. He took Abhishek's catch earlier, now takes Iyer's catch. Safe hands in the field. Probably a blessing in disguise for India as Shreyas wasn't able to kick on. Naman Dhir, right handed bat, comes to the crease

Keemo Paul to Naman Dhir, SIX, that's a first ball maximum for Naman Dhir! Looks like he was batting in the nets before walking in to bat. Picks the bones out of this back of a length delivery, whipping it over deep square leg for half-a-dozen. That came right off the meat of the bat

Keemo Paul to Naman Dhir, FOUR, he's off to a brisk start. Already 10 runs in 2 balls. This was slow, short and wide outside off, allows Naman Dhir to free his arms. He thumps it over mid-off, has enough elevation to clear the fielder as the ball races away to the boundary
Keemo Paul to Naman Dhir, wide, under pressure he has fired a short and wide ball outside off, out of Naman Dhir's reach

Keemo Paul to Naman Dhir, SIX, 100 up for India! A good length delivery outside off, slight width on offer, Naman Dhir effortlessly lofts it over long-off for six more. That was middled to perfection, and was all about timing. Should have been promoted up the order in this rain curtailed contest
Keemo Paul to Naman Dhir, 1 run, full and quick on middle and leg, Naman Dhir flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a single

Keemo Paul to Tilak Varma, 2 runs, back of a length delivery around middle and leg, Tilak Varma loses his shape while going for a pull, miscues it towards mid-wicket as the fielder charges in from the deep. Doesn't carry, as there wasn't enough power of timing behind the shot
